matchups.analysis: Doakes22's dead in the water at 1% win probability with 91.1 final points locked in, getting absolutely demolished by espnfan7338848211's projected 128.0 finish—that's a 37-point beatdown where the only thing keeping this from being a complete blowout is the fact that espnfan still has Jaxson Dart and Rams D/ST left to play. The real killer is benching TreVeyon Henderson (13.6) for Saquon Barkley's pathetic 3.0 points, which cost you 10.6 points you absolutely needed when you're already getting stomped—that's the difference between looking slightly less embarrassed and whatever this is. Saquon projecting 17.6 and delivering 3.0 is inexplicable, but at least you've got Brandon Aubrey outperforming by 6.4 points to cushion the blow slightly; espnfan's Ja'Marr Chase going absolutely nuclear at 26.5 (projected 19.0) basically sealed your fate before halftime. This one's over except for the formality of final scores hitting.

SteelerFan9828's completely cooked at 93.9 with a 0% win probability, and this one was decided the moment you benched George Kittle for Colston Loveland and watched that 16.7-point swing evaporate—you literally had an extra touchdown sitting on your bench while your actual starter contributed basically nothing. Caleb Williams finished at 7.7 when ESPN had him at 19.4, so your young QB stack decided to underperform at exactly the wrong time, but that's almost secondary to the fact that you made a catastrophically bad start/sit call that cost you nearly a full touchdown before either guy took another snap. 82Cole47's running away at 135.4 with 100% win probability, which means Josh Allen's 18-point beat on projection was basically the dagger—Cole's just got safer remaining execution across the board and the projection cushion to prove it. You maxed out Amon-Ra for 35.2 and now need eight more guys to collectively bail you out of a decision that shouldn't have needed bailing out in the first place.

Eric Brotmann's walking away with this one at 99% and ESPN's projecting him to finish at 135.1 while you're staring down 81.9—that's a 53-point gap that tells you everything you need to know about how badly this one got away from you. CeeDee Lamb absolutely carried you on his back with 35.3 points while Bijan Robinson decided to be a fucking afterthought at 11.1 instead of the 22.9 he was supposed to hit, so you're already down 11.8 points before we even get to the real disaster: you benched Khalil Shakir's 6.8 points to start Quentin Johnston's 2.4-point dud, which is a -4.4 swing that cost you a roster spot you didn't have to lose. Eric's sitting pretty with CeeDee already eating, and yeah, he fucked up benching Dalton Kincaid's 22.5 for Rhamondre Stevenson's 3.6, but he's got such a massive cushion that even his own incompetence barely dents his win probability—you needed a miracle this week and instead got a masterclass in how not to manage a roster. With Harrison Mevis your only remaining play and Eric still having Kyren Williams and Isaiah Likely to pad the lead, this one's done.

ESPNFAN6437471416's already got this locked at 115.9 with 100% win probability, which is what happens when Brock Purdy decides to actually beat his projection by 7.9 points instead of being the mid-range option everyone drafted him to be. But here's the thing that's going to haunt espn88256878 all week: benching Patrick Mahomes (29.0) to start Jalen Hurts (16.2) cost you 12.8 fucking points, and that's the difference between this being close and getting absolutely embarrassed by a full touchdown with Puka Nacua still pending. Javonte Williams also decided to show up as a liability at 8.0 when you needed 16.7, so you're running double dead weight on a roster that's already buried before your last starter even takes the field. espn88256878 somehow out-projected Hurts with Kelce (25.1 vs 10.5) and still got smoked because the rest of your lineup made decisions that belong in a Reddit post titled "How I Lost My League," and now you're watching the clock tick on a loss that was fully self-inflicted before halftime Sunday.

RGM2215's down 34.1 points with Malik Nabers as the only lifeline, and ESPN's got them at 1% because that's basically what happens when you bench Jake Ferguson for 20.3 points to start DK Metcalf's 6.7-point corpse—that's a 13.6-point swing you're trying to overcome before your remaining guy even catches a snap. ESPNfan's sitting at 99% win probability with everyone already in the books at 133.2, which means you needed your entire remaining stack to go absolutely nuclear while also praying their already-locked scores somehow retroactively got lower, and neither of those things are happening. Jameson Williams also decided to be completely useless at 5.3 when he was supposed to be 12.3, so you're buried in self-inflicted holes while ESPNfan's already celebrating—Nabers would need a 35-point monster game just to make this competitive, and that's not the math that usually works out when you're down this far with one guy left.
